hero.lede: We develop the Triangular Spatial Relationship (TSR) method for comparing biomolecular 3D structures without alignment. TSR represents structures as integer keys; our software, BioTSR, computes these keys for structural comparison and clustering.

researchVision.heading: Toward Deciphering Molecular Recognition
researchVision.question: Is there a general molecular recognition code that governs how biomolecules recognize one another and how those interactions reshape molecular structure?
researchVision.body: Comparing TSR keys across structures can identify conserved, altered and interaction-associated spatial patterns. Our long-term goal is to combine these interpretable descriptors with machine learning, AI-generated structures and simulation-derived ensembles to connect structure prediction with mechanistic understanding.

software.heading: BioTSR
software.intro: BioTSR provides Python and command-line tools for computing TSR keys and comparing structures through their shared keys.
highlights: Proteins (Cα or heavy atoms), ligands, carbohydrates and nucleotides, and the interface between two molecules (cross TSR).
Whole datasets from one CSV manifest, processed in parallel.
Common keys from the command line; similarity, clustering and a clustered heat map from Python.

research.heading: Methods & research
research.intro: The core representation has been extended to amino acids, drugs, ligands, nucleotides and the interfaces between molecules. Each method and analysis has its own page, with the paper behind it.
research.methodsCard: Amino-acid grouping, mirror images, size filtering, secondary structure, amino acids, drugs, nucleotides and nucleotide–protein interfaces.
research.analysisCard: Finding the keys structures share, clustering structures by key similarity, and models trained on key frequencies.
research.earlierCard: The programs the methods were first published with, and separate tools written for particular papers.
